g1.label: 1. The traffic on the Brooklyn Bridge is bad during rush hour.
g1.why: Right. David starts with “It’s always bad on the Brooklyn Bridge during rush hour.”

g2.label: 2. David lives in downtown Manhattan.
g2.why: Wrong. He says “I live in Queens, but I like to work in downtown Manhattan.” He works there — he does not live there.

g3.label: 3. In the 1920s the Empire State Building was the tallest building in the world.
g3.why: Wrong. The text says “They built it in the early 1930s”, not the 1920s.

g4.label: 4. There’s a zoo in Central Park.
g4.why: Right. In Central Park there are “trees, lakes, playgrounds, a zoo and lots more.”

g5.label: 5. The Metropolitan Museum of Art had 102 pieces of art when it opened.
g5.why: Wrong. The museum opened with 174 pieces of art. 102 is the number of stories in the Empire State Building.

g6.label: 6. David thinks you can buy the best hot dogs from a hot dog cart.
g6.why: Right. His friend Nick has a hot dog cart and “he does the best hot dogs in New York”.

g1.label: Odd one out 1: public transport · shopping mall · rush hour · traffic jam
g1.why: Public transport, rush hour and traffic jam are all about traffic. A shopping mall is a place to go shopping.

g2.label: Odd one out 2: skyline · skyscraper · subway · tower
g2.why: A skyline, a skyscraper and a tower are all high above the street. The subway runs under it.

g3.label: Odd one out 3: intersection · campsite · roadwork · road sign
g3.why: An intersection, roadwork and a road sign all belong to a road. A campsite is where you put up a tent.

g4.label: Odd one out 4: sightseeing · sidewalk · tourist · visitor
g4.why: Sightseeing, a tourist and a visitor are all about people visiting a place. A sidewalk is the part of the street you walk on.

m1.label: Match 1: a place where they are building something
m1.why: A construction site is the place where something is being built.

m2.label: Match 2: people live here, away from the city center
m2.why: The suburbs are the areas around a city, away from the centre.

m3.label: Match 3: you can leave your car here
m3.why: A parking lot is where you leave your car.

m4.label: Match 4: a person who travels to work every day
m4.why: A commuter is someone who travels to work and back every day.

r1.label: Revision 1: famous statue in New York harbour
r1.why: The Statue of Liberty stands on an island in New York harbour. The Golden Gate Bridge is in San Francisco.

r2.label: Revision 2: American holiday in November
r2.why: Thanksgiving is the November holiday when American families eat turkey together. Halloween is on 31 October.

g1.label: 1. underground (BE) →
g1.why: British underground = American subway. In London you take the tube; in New York you take the subway.

g2.label: 2. car park (BE) →
g2.why: British car park = American parking lot.

g3.label: 3. town centre (BE) →
g3.why: British town centre = American downtown. David says he likes to work in downtown Manhattan.

g5.label: 5. lift (BE) →
g5.why: British lift = American elevator. An escalator is the moving staircase, which is different.

g6.label: 6. Which spelling is American English?
g6.why: American English drops the u in colour and swaps -re for -er: color, theater, favorite.
